summary.en-US: Sends the files you download in Firefox to DasIDM, a free and open-source download manager for Windows: many connections per file, resume, torrents and video. Needs the DasIDM app.

description.en-US: DasIDM – Download Manager hands the files you download in Firefox to DasIDM, a free, open-source download manager for Windows 10 and 11. Get the app from https://github.com/ApurvDas/dasidm/releases/latest What it does • When you download a file, DasIDM opens with the file filled in. Press Enter and it downloads over up to 32 connections, with pause, resume and crash safety. • Files behind a login work: the add-on passes the site's cookie and referrer to DasIDM. • Alt+click a link to keep that one download in Firefox. Right-click any link for "Download with DasIDM". • If DasIDM isn't running, it starts; if it can't take a download, Firefox simply keeps it. • The toolbar button shows whether DasIDM is connected, and turns capture off, private windows on, or a minimum file size. Privacy The add-on talks only to DasIDM on your own PC, through Firefox's native messaging. Nothing is sent to any server, there is no telemetry, and private windows are left alone unless you allow them. Full policy: https://github.com/ApurvDas/dasidm/blob/main/PRIVACY.md DasIDM is not affiliated with Internet Download Manager or Tonec Inc.

version.approval_notes:
This add-on is the browser half of DasIDM, an open-source Windows download manager (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/ApurvDas/dasidm . Source of this add-on: extension/firefox in that repository. Plain JavaScript, no build step, no minified, bundled or remote code.

HOW TO TEST (Windows 10/11)
1. Install DasIDM from https://github.com/ApurvDas/dasidm/releases/latest (DasIDM_<version>_x64-setup.exe, per-user, no admin). Start it once: it registers its native messaging host (HKCU\Software\Mozilla\NativeMessagingHosts\dev.dasidm.host -> %LOCALAPPDATA%\DasIDM\browser\dev.dasidm.host.json, pointing at DasIDM.exe).
2. Click the toolbar button: it should say "Connected".
3. Download any file (for example https://proof.ovh.net/files/1Mb.dat). DasIDM comes to the front with the file filled in, and Firefox's own download is cancelled. Press Enter in DasIDM to download it.
4. Alt+click a download link: Firefox keeps that download. Turn "Grab downloads" off in the popup: Firefox keeps every download.

PERMISSIONS
- nativeMessaging: hands a download (URL, file name, size, the site's Cookie / Referer / User-Agent) to DasIDM.exe on the same PC. Nothing leaves the computer.
- webRequest, webRequestBlocking, <all_urls>: reads response headers of top-level and frame loads to tell files (Content-Disposition: attachment, or types Firefox can't display) from pages, and cancels a request only after DasIDM has accepted it. Firefox add-on files (.xpi) are never taken.
- downloads: catches downloads the step above can't see (download links, script downloads), pauses them, and erases them once DasIDM has them, or resumes them if not.
- cookies: so downloads behind a login keep working in DasIDM.
- contextMenus: "Download with DasIDM" on links. storage: the popup's three settings.
The content script only listens for Alt+click on links (to leave that download to Firefox).

If DasIDM is not installed or not running, the add-on fails open: Firefox downloads as usual.
